lists.findOrCreate: Find a list, or name a new one
lists.name: List name
lists.emptyList: Nothing in this list yet. Add a book from its own page.
lists.emptyTag: Nothing under this tag any more.
lists.deleteConfirm: {{name}} goes; the books in it stay on the shelf.

draw.hint: For a book no catalog has a cover for. Write the prompt from the book first, then draw it.
draw.noKey: Drawing needs an OpenAI key — the other vendors here cannot make images.

identify.title: Lookup
identify.hint: Cover, title, author, year and ISBN, from Open Library and Google Books.
identify.what: Covers and details from Open Library and Google Books. Picking one fills in the cover, the title, the author, the year and the ISBN.
identify.none: Nothing came back. Try the fuller title, or add the author.

shelf.title: Shelf
shelf.unreadable: The library could not be opened. Nothing has been lost — the books are still on the device.
shelf.fromLinkHint: A Google Doc, or any direct file URL
shelf.linkHint: A Google Doc link comes in as .docx. The file must be readable without signing in.
shelf.linkSignIn: That link asked us to sign in. Share it as "anyone with the link", or download it and import the file.
shelf.kindTitle: What kind of book is this?

import.title: Import
import.noText: No text found in this file. If it's a scanned PDF, the pages are images — we can't read those.
import.previewEmpty: Nothing readable came out. If the pages are scans, they're images.

book.deleteConfirm: Delete this book? Its notes and highlights go with it.
book.title: Title
book.author: Author
book.summaryPlaceholder: What is this book about? A few sentences.
book.aiSummarizeWhat: Writes a few sentences from the chapter briefs where they exist, and from the opening where they don't. Yours is replaced, so copy it first if you want to keep it.
book.esvKeyHint: What the chapters are fetched with. Kept in the keychain on this device.
book.correctHint: Title, author, year and edition, as they should read.
book.correctWhat: Reads back the title, author, year and edition as they should be for this work, and corrects what is wrong — a title typed from memory, an author down to an initial, a missing subtitle, a year off by one. It never translates a title or turns the record into a different book, and a work it cannot identify comes back saying so. One small request.
book.correctQueued: Asked. Watch it in the queue.
book.summarizeWhat: Writes the book's summary from the briefs its chapters already carry. Nothing of the text is sent, and nothing is read twice — so this costs one small request however long the book is.
book.summarizeQueued: Asked. Watch it in the queue.
book.partsHint: Each one has its own page — what it is, its chapters, and every note you made inside it.
book.notRated: Tap a star. Tap it again to clear it.
book.reviewPlaceholder: What did you make of it?
book.impressionsPlaceholder: A quick overview of the whole book — what it was, and what stayed with you.
book.lookUpWhat: Asks for the author, the year and a few sentences on what this book is, from the model's own knowledge of it. Only what the shelf is missing is filled in, and a book it does not know comes back saying so rather than invented.
book.outlineHint: The chapter list of a book whose pages are not here.
book.outlineWhat: Asks for this book's table of contents — every chapter in order, each with a line on what it covers. Then every chapter has a page of its own to make notes on. A book the model does not know comes back saying so.
book.outlineQueued: Asked. Watch it in the queue.
book.outlineReplace: This replaces the {{count}} chapters already here, and anything you corrected in them.

reader.copyHint: The passage, and where it is from.
reader.hint: Tap any sentence to highlight, note or share it.
reader.notePlaceholder: What do you want to remember about this?
reader.shareCardHint: A themed page in your reading colors.

settings.title: Settings
settings.aiHint: Used by chapter detection and analysis. Keys never leave this device, including in backups.
settings.cloudHint: Storage you own. Off by default.
settings.backupHint: Survives a bad import or a corrupt database — not a lost phone. Copy the file off to keep it safe.
settings.aiGetOne: Don't have a {{vendor}} key? Get one →
settings.aiBilling: Requests are billed to your own {{vendor}} account.
settings.aiStrategyHint: Order is the fallback order. Sequential stays on the first key until it errors; round robin spreads every call.
settings.privateCloudHint: Storage you own. Off by default.
settings.gradeHint_fast: 512px on the older model. Quick and cheap, and the loosest with what the prompt asked for.
settings.gradeHint_normal: 1024px, cheapest pass of the current model. Follows the prompt closely.
settings.gradeHint_best: 1024px at the slowest pass. Same obedience, more of everything else.
settings.removeAllWarning: A uniquely named backup will be saved locally and, when configured, to iCloud and each connected S3 bucket. iCloud backups omit manuscript text. Deletion starts after the backups finish; if a cloud backup fails, your data remains.

job.title: Getting it
job.working: This stays here while it works. It opens by itself when the book is ready.
job.hint: You can leave — it keeps going, and the shelf shows the same progress.
job.failedHint: Nothing was added. Retry sends the same request again.

lookup.keyStaysHere: The key stays on this device — never synced, never in a backup.
lookup.savedHint: Only what you looked up, and only on this device.
lookup.busy: The source is rate-limiting. Try again shortly.
lookup.rejected: That key was rejected. Check it at api.esv.org.
lookup.offline: Couldn’t reach api.esv.org. This one needs a signal.

entity.noRenderings: Not named in any other language yet.
entity.name: Name
entity.summaryPlaceholder: Who are they, in a line or two?
entity.timelineFetched: Counted from the text on this device. This edition arrives a chapter at a time, so a graph would show where you have read rather than where they appear.
entity.polishWhat: Turns {{count}} chapter notes about this person into a profile: summary, role, appearance, voice and arc. The per-chapter notes stay as they are underneath, so you can run it again or check what it drew on.
entity.tapToRead: Tap a line to read it where it happens.
entity.relationSearch: Search people, or type a new name
entity.relationEmpty: Nobody else in this book yet.

notes.empty: Highlights and notes you make while reading show up here.
notes.selectHint: Tap the ones you want gone.
notes.deleteSelectedConfirm: Delete {{count}} marks? The words stay in the book.
notes.emptyRecord: No notes yet. Tap ＋ to write one about this book.

structure.deleteWhere: Its text has to join a chapter. Which one?
structure.title: Structure
structure.unsureCount: {{count}} chapters the detector wasn't sure about.
structure.redetectConfirm: Re-run detection? Chapters you renamed keep their names.
structure.redetectHint: Your renames and splits survive a re-run; everything else is recomputed.
structure.splitHint: The sentence you pick begins the new chapter. ¶ marks a paragraph start.
structure.noSplitPoints: This chapter is a single paragraph — there's nowhere to split it.
structure.aiDetectWhat: Sends only the short lines that could be headings — never the manuscript — and asks which are chapters. Your renames are kept.
structure.aiFoundNothing: No chapters found. Nothing was changed.
structure.deleteConfirm: Its text joins the neighbouring chapter. Nothing is removed from the manuscript.
structure.aiScenes: Suggest scene breaks in every chapter
structure.aiScenesWhat: Sends the first line of each paragraph — never the prose — and asks where the time, place or viewpoint changes. Chapters you've already marked are overwritten.
structure.aiChapterBrief: Write this chapter's brief with AI
structure.aiOneWhat: Reads this one chapter with the book's summary, the chapters just before it, and everyone already known as context. Writes its brief, its people, its places and the ties between them.
structure.aiOneBriefWhat: One or two sentences on what happens, written with the chapters just before it as context.
structure.addChapterHint: Goes on the end, unnamed. Open it to give it a name and a note.
structure.recordHint: There is no text here to split, so the chapters are the ones you type or the ones the model knows. Briefs are written from what it knows of the book, and it says so when it does not know it.

backup.title: Backup
backup.icloudOff: iCloud Drive is off on this device
backup.icloudDirections: Settings → your name → iCloud → iCloud Drive → turn on
backup.icloudUnsigned: This build of the app isn't signed for iCloud.
backup.waiting: {{count}} books are waiting for their file
backup.icloudBrowseHint: Ten copies are kept, newest first. Restoring adds those books beside the ones you have; it never overwrites them.
backup.nowUnchanged: Nothing has changed since the last copy.
backup.waitingDetail: Import the same file again and its notes, profiles and chapters come back with it.
backup.restoredWaiting: {{count}} books need their file imported again.
backup.fileHint: One .zip file holds your books, structure, notes and profiles — open it anywhere. It never contains an AI key.
backup.restoreConfirm: Restoring adds books; it never overwrites what's already here.
backup.duplicates: Already on your shelf, restored as copies: {{list}}
backup.unplaceable_no-text: {{title}} had no text and was skipped.
backup.notABundle: That isn't a Novel Man backup.
backup.tooNew: This backup was made by a newer version (v{{version}}). Update the app first.

ai.canceled: Stopped. What had already finished was kept.
ai.noKey: No AI key configured. Add one in Settings first.
ai.estimateHint: An estimate, not a quote. Billed to your own account. Results are cached, so a repeat run is free.
ai.estimateNoKey: add an AI key to see the cost
ai.estimateForCited: {{action}} · est. {{tokens}} tokens · {{cost}} — the title, this chapter's place in it and what the shelf already knows. There is no text here to send.

cast.hint: Each pass reads the book once and caches what it learns, so running it again costs nothing for the parts that haven't changed.
cast.what_relations: Asks how the people who share chapters are connected. Sends profiles, not the manuscript.
cast.what_continuity: Compares what different chapters said about the same person and flags what disagrees. Flags are suggestions to review, never edits.
cast.extracted: {{characters}} people across the book. {{failed}} chapters failed.
cast.flagged: {{count}} things to look at. {{failed}} people failed.
cast.graphHint: Tap a person to isolate them. Hold to open their profile. Drag to move the graph.
cast.clearConfirm: Removes generated profiles, appearances, relationships and flags. Profiles you wrote yourself stay.

translate.empty: Add a language to translate this book into. Nothing is sent anywhere until you run it.
translate.mappingShort: Names and terms these translations must obey.
translate.fromChapter: Translated a chapter at a time, from the chapter you are reading.
translate.nothingYet: Nothing translated in this chapter yet.
translate.editHint: Tap a sentence to correct it. A correction is kept as an example for the ones after it, and can be promoted to a mapping.
translate.readInReader: Read it in the reader — the Aa menu chooses the language.
translate.promoteHint: A term is obeyed in every chapter, and the sentences already using it are marked for re-running.
translate.termAffects: {{count}} translated sentences use it and are now marked for re-running.
translate.termsHint: Every mapping here is obeyed exactly, everywhere this language is written. ✨ proposes one for every name that has none — a draft to read and correct before anything is saved.
translate.someFailed: Kept the {{count}} that came back. The rest stopped at: {{error}}
translate.proposedHint: Nothing is saved yet. Correct what is wrong, drop what you do not want, then keep or reject the lot.
translate.nothingToFill: Every term here already has a translation.
translate.suggestNone: Nothing came back it was sure of.
translate.candidates: Found in the text, not mapped yet
translate.candidatesHint: Names and repeated proper nouns the app found by reading the book. Tap one to put it in the row above and give it a translation.
translate.removeConfirm: Delete the {{language}} translation, including your edits?

cloud.title: Cloud backup
cloud.hint: iCloud keeps what you made — notes, people, progress, settings — and not the books. A bucket you own keeps everything, manuscripts included, and nothing goes up until you ask.
cloud.addConnectionHint: An S3-compatible bucket of your own, for a history that keeps everything.
cloud.name: Name
cloud.pasteHint: Paste a console block, an .env chunk or a CSV row and the fields fill themselves in.
cloud.saveHint: Saving makes a real request. A bucket that can't be listed isn't saved.
cloud.frequencyHint: Manual by default. Automatic syncs run when you open the app, never in the background.
cloud.getHint: Getting a bundle restores it the same way a file does — it adds, it never overwrites.
cloud.removeConfirm: Removes the connection and its key from this device. Nothing in the bucket is touched.

script.hint: One pass per scene, so the split you made in the structure editor is the split the screenplay gets.
script.what: Turns each scene into slug lines, action and dialogue. Interior thoughts become what a camera could see, which is a real rewrite — read it before you use it.
script.clearConfirm: Deletes the converted screenplay. The novel is untouched.

work.title: Analysis queue
work.hint: Work carries on while you read, and picks up where it left off if you close the app. Finished chapters are kept even if a run is stopped.
work.queued: Queued {{count}} chapters. Watch it on the shelf.
work.seeWhat: Tap to see what it did

chapter.title: Chapter
chapter.noScenes: No scenes yet — mark one, or let an analysis read for them.
chapter.hint: Names here open that profile. Analyzing the chapter fills the scenes, the people, the places and how those people are tied to each other.
chapter.scriptHint: The scenes of this book as a screenplay.
chapter.recapWhose: Written from a model’s memory of this book, not from the book itself. Check anything that matters.
chapter.noTerms: No terms recognized in this chapter.
chapter.noNotes: Nothing written about this chapter yet.

part.hint: Notes are kept at the verse where you made them, so this page collects the ones that fall inside this book.

keyLog.title: AI key
keyLog.empty: Nothing sent with this key yet.
keyLog.hint: Only requests that actually went out are here — a cached answer costs nothing and is not sent. The last 300 are kept, and the key itself is never stored in this log.
keyLog.clearConfirm: Delete the request history for this key?
keyLog.modelCustomHint: Type an id the list is missing and press done. Priced as an estimate.
keyLog.modelHint: This key runs on the model picked here. A cheaper model is fine for a first sweep; a stronger one reads scenes and people out of a chapter far more reliably.

scenes.title: Scenes
scenes.emptyHint: Scenes come from analyzing a chapter, or from marking a break yourself in the chapter list. Nothing is guessed at import.
scenes.noSummary: No summary for this one yet.

place.timelineFetched: Counted from the text on this device. This edition arrives a chapter at a time, so a graph would show where you have read rather than where it appears.
place.name: Name
place.summaryPlaceholder: A line or two about this place.
place.noMentions: Not recorded in any chapter yet.
place.hint: A place is filled in by analyzing the chapters it appears in. Everything here can be edited or added by hand.
place.polishWhat: Turns {{count}} chapter notes about this place into a profile: what it is, what it is like, and what happens there. The per-chapter notes stay as they are underneath, so you can run it again or check what it drew on.

scene.timelineFetched: Counted from the text on this device. This edition arrives a chapter at a time, so there is nothing here to count yet.
scene.title: Scene
scene.hint: Who is in a scene is counted from the scene's own words, so a name only mentioned elsewhere in the chapter does not appear here.

source.ebibleDetail: Bibles, in the editions this app offers
source.gutenbergDetail: 79,000 books out of copyright, as EPUB
source.arxivDetail: Open-access papers: physics, computing, mathematics, biology, economics
source.arxivHint: Search arXiv by subject, title or author — or pick a category and read what was filed there most recently.
source.standardebooksDetail: The same out-of-copyright books, typeset and proofread by hand
source.repoDetail: Bibles other people keep on GitHub — the editions no catalog is allowed to carry
source.repoHint: Search for a version, then paste the link to the file you found
source.openlibraryDetail: 40 million books, catalogued — records to keep notes against, not files to read
source.openlibraryHint: Keep a category once and search it offline, or search all of Open Library while you have a signal.
source.goodreadsDetail: Your own shelves, ratings and reviews, brought over
source.goodreadsHint: Their API was retired, so this reads the export file or your shelf's RSS feed.

find.prompt: Type what you are looking for, then Search.
find.localPrompt: Type a title or an author. Searches the lists on this device: {{sources}}.
find.failed: Couldn’t reach the source. Try again in a moment.

kind.novelHint: Fiction — people, scenes, screenplay and illustrations
kind.scriptureHint: A bible — real people and places, verses, and references. Downloaded from eBible.org.
kind.nonfictionHint: Real people and places, read as record — no scenes or screenplay
kind.textbookHint: A book you learn from — a course text, a manual, a tutorial. Sections and notes, no people or places.
kind.paperHint: One academic paper. Sections rather than chapters, and a pass that weighs what it claims.

add.free: Nothing is fetched until you tap this.
add.gutenbergWhat: The EPUB without plates — the same words, a fraction of the size.
add.paperWhat: The PDF arXiv serves, read through the text extractor — you see what it found before it becomes a book.
add.indexMissing: No list yet — fetch it once, then search it offline
add.esvWhy: Licensed by Crossway and not downloadable — but with a key of your own you can look up any passage.
add.esvAddWhat: All 66 books and 1,189 chapters. Each chapter is fetched when you open it, then kept for reading offline.
add.updateFailed: Couldn't reach eBible.org. The list you already have still works.
add.searchEditions: A name, a language, an abbreviation
add.noTranslations: None of the editions this app offers are in the list right now.
add.canonAllHint: The deuterocanonical books this edition carries.
add.structureIncluded: Structure included — its chapters and verses are published, not detected.
add.standardebooksWhat: One EPUB, with the chapters its own spine states — nothing here has to guess them.
add.seWhy: Their feeds are a membership benefit, so the credential has to be yours — this app has none to give.
add.seStaysHere: The address stays on this device — never synced, never in a backup.
add.seHowToGet: Access comes with a donation to the Patrons Circle, with producing an ebook for them, or with a sponsorship. standardebooks.org/feeds/opds says which.
add.se_no-email: Add your Patrons Circle email first.
add.se_rejected: That address was refused. Feed access needs a current membership.
add.se_offline: Couldn’t reach standardebooks.org. This one needs a signal.
add.se_no-feed: Their feed answered but listed no catalog to read.
add.recordRow: Keep everything of a book but content
add.recordWhy: One you read on paper, borrowed, or mean to read. No text — a shelf entry for your rating, your review and your notes.
add.recordHint: You can ask AI for the contents and a summary from its page afterwards, where it knows the book.
add.recordWhat: The record only: title, author, year and cover. Open Library has no copy of the book to give, and neither will this.
add.pickOne: Pick one of the three above, or type a title.
add.recordLookUp: Add it, then ask AI what it is

graph.barScale: Each bar covers {{count}} chapters — tap one

repo.title: A bible on GitHub
repo.searchPlaceholder: niv, nkjv, 和合本 — a version or a language
repo.searchWhat: Opens your browser: repositories, most-starred first
repo.searchHint: There is no list of these to keep, so this searches where they live. It looks for “bible” and whatever you typed.
repo.readWhat: The page you were reading or the raw file — either works. Nothing is downloaded yet.
repo.formats: Reads JSON and XML: one file per book, or a whole bible in one file. Its chapters and verses come from the file rather than from guesswork.
repo.perBook: One file per book, fetched in the canon’s order
repo.yours: A repository is somebody’s copy, not the publisher’s edition. Whether it may be copied is between you and whoever holds the rights.
repo.what: Structure included — its chapters and verses are stated in the file, not detected.
repo.err_url: That is not a GitHub link to a file, a folder or a repository.
repo.err_missing: Nothing is at that path. Check the branch and the file name.
repo.err_limited: GitHub is rate-limiting this device. It lifts within the hour.
repo.err_offline: Couldn’t reach GitHub. This one needs a signal.
repo.err_nothing: That folder holds no bible this can read. Link one file inside it instead.
repo.err_shape: Nothing in “{{detail}}” is laid out as books, chapters and verses. It reads JSON and XML that are.
repo.err_canon: “{{detail}}” can be read, but what is in it is not a bible — its books and chapter counts match no canon.

term.name: Name
term.summaryPlaceholder: A line or two about what this is.
term.noUses: Not recorded in any chapter yet.
term.hint: Terms are filled in by analyzing the chapters they appear in. Everything here can be edited or added by hand.

ol.searchLive: A title or an author — then return
ol.hintKept: Everything in the categories you have kept. Type to narrow it.
ol.hintLive: Searches openlibrary.org as you ask it. Needs a signal.
ol.categoriesHint: A category is fetched once and searched on the device after that — no signal needed.
ol.getFailed: Couldn't reach openlibrary.org. The categories you already have still work.
ol.noLists: No category kept yet. Get one below, or search all of Open Library.
ol.whatYouGet: Adding one gives you the record — title, author, year and cover. Not the book.

gr.noApi: Goodreads switched their API off in 2020, so nothing can sign in on your behalf. What they still give you is an export of your library and an RSS feed per shelf — both carry your ratings and reviews.
gr.how1: On goodreads.com: My Books › Import and export › Export Library
gr.how1Detail: They email you a CSV, or put a download link on that page. Save it to Files, then choose it here.
gr.notAnExport: No books in that file. Make sure it is the library export and not the reviews one.
gr.feedWhy: The only door that opens twice: re-read it whenever the shelf changes, no export needed.
gr.feedHint: On your shelf page, the RSS link at the bottom. It carries a key of its own, so keep it to yourself.
gr.notAFeed: That is not a Goodreads shelf feed address.
gr.feedFailed: Couldn't read that feed. Check the address, or use the export.
gr.whatHappens: Each one becomes a shelf entry with no text: its rating, its review, its shelf and its private notes. A book already here is filled in rather than added twice, and nothing you have written is overwritten.
gr.filledHint: Already on the shelf, and missing something the export had.

status.readHint: Finished with it — or finished trying.

gallery.title: Gallery
gallery.queued: It joins the queue — leave the page, it keeps going.
